text:
The snapshot looks like January 2015.

- Unemployment is 5.6%, which matches December 2014 or January 2015.
- Headline CPI is 0.66% YoY, which fits oil falling sharply. December 2014 headline CPI was 0.8% and January 2015 was -0.1%. Because "latest published" may lag, the data could be January with December CPI, or the end of December.
- The 10-year yield is 1.77%, which fits late January 2015 (about 1.64% at month end) better than December 2014 (2.17%). A 3-month drop of -0.58 from about 2.35 in October gives 1.77, so this looks like it could be January 2015 using an average, or possibly a different date.
- The 20+ year Treasury return of +10% in one month matches January 2015, when long bonds surged.
- US large-cap equity fell 3.9% in the month, which matches January 2015 (S&P -3.0%).
- The broad dollar is up 9.66% YoY, which fits early 2015.
- Gold gained 7.2% in the month, which matches January 2015.
- The VIX at 18.76 fits January 2015.

The 10-year yield is the weakest fit, but everything else points to January 2015.
